title: Adiabatically-induced Kawaguchi geometry and jerk in quantum-classical systems
authors: Athanasios Chatzistavrakidis, Larisa Jonke, Ryan Requist
abstract: Adiabatically eliminating the quantum degrees of freedom in a mixed quantum-classical system produces an effective force in the classical equation of motion. The elimination can be made to any order in the adiabatic parameter, generating a series of higher order forces. By applying a sequence of near-identity unitary transformations to the quantum state, we derive a hierarchy of increasingly accurate effective actions for the classical variables. The third order Euler-Lagrange equation is non-Newtonian as the force depends on the jerk, the third order time derivative of position. We find that the third order terms induce a special kind of Kawaguchi geometry on the space of classical variables. This geometry is characterized by an almost symplectic structure and a differential line element that depends on the acceleration in addition to the velocity. Our results can be used to efficiently capture higher order nonadiabatic effects in molecular dynamics simulations.
summary: The paper develops an advanced theoretical method to model quantum-classical systems by adiabatically eliminating fast electronic degrees of freedom. It derives increasingly accurate effective equations of motion, culminating in a description governed by Kawaguchi geometry due to third-order nonadiabatic forces involving the jerk. This provides a powerful geometric tool for simulating complex molecular dynamics beyond standard approximations.
main_problem: To derive an effective equation of motion for slow classical variables by adiabatically eliminating fast quantum degrees of freedom, incorporating nonadiabatic effects up to the third order.
main_result: The resulting dynamics are governed by a geometry characterized by Kawaguchi geometry (or KL2 manifolds), leading to equations involving the jerk ($\ddot{x}$'s derivative) rather than just acceleration.
method: Adiabatic perturbation theory is used iteratively, employing near-identity unitary transformations to systematically derive higher-order effective actions and Hamiltonians from the full quantum-classical action functional.
model_or_system: The system models mixed quantum-classical dynamics (e.g., molecular systems) where electronic states $|\psiangle$ evolve quantum mechanically based on a Hamiltonian $H(x)$ dependent on classical nuclear coordinates $x_\mu$.

why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous geometric framework for nonadiabatic dynamics that goes significantly beyond standard Born-Oppenheimer or even generalized geodesic approaches by incorporating higher-order time derivatives into the effective Lagrangian/Hamiltonian structure.
